edges.explanation: Both predict action sequences to manage the control horizon, but CVAE chunking and diffusion are different policy distributions, not successive checkpoints.
Octo describes itself as a transformer-based diffusion policy scaled through diverse robot pretraining.
RT-2 succeeds RT-1 in the same research line but changes to a pretrained VLM and text-form actions; this is not RT-1 weight continuation.
RT-1-X applies the RT-1 architecture to cross-embodiment data.
RT-2-X is the VLM-based RT-X instantiation.
Octo pretraining uses the Open X-Embodiment dataset; RT-X weights are not the Octo backbone.
edges.endpoint_note: The cited reuse is the OXE dataset, not RT-X policy weights.

edges.explanation: OpenVLA uses the Open X-Embodiment data ecosystem while choosing its own VLM architecture.
edges.endpoint_note: The cited reuse is the OXE dataset, not RT-X policy weights.

edges.explanation: Both map VLM features to discretized autoregressive actions; similarity is architectural, not proof of inherited private RT-2 weights.
OFT modifies OpenVLA fine-tuning and action decoding while retaining its pretrained foundation.
pi0-FAST uses FAST tokenization to instantiate an autoregressive variant; FAST itself is a representation method.
edges.endpoint_note: The explicit variant is the pi0-FAST policy; FAST alone denotes the tokenizer.

edges.explanation: pi0.5 builds on pi0 and adds heterogeneous training and hierarchical task behavior.
Knowledge insulation uses FAST action tokens as an auxiliary learning signal for the VLM backbone.
The pi0.6 model card explicitly builds on pi0.5 while changing backbone, action expert and data.
RECAP trains pi0.6 with offline and on-robot RL, yielding pi-star-0.6.
The memory experiments augment pi0.6 with visual and language memory.
pi0.7 retains the pi0.6 architectural foundation and changes context conditioning.
pi0.7 uses the MEM-style visual-history encoder and memory system.
pi0.7 uses experience from RL-trained specialists with strategy metadata to absorb their behaviors.
Both couple VLM features to flow action generation, but GR00T uses cross-attention and embodiment adapters; they do not share published checkpoints.
The GR00T N1 paper explicitly cites ACT for action chunking.
N1.5 modifies the VLM, data and future-feature objective relative to N1.
N1.6 replaces/updates the backbone, enlarges the DiT and changes action representations.
The repository positions N1.7 as the next N1 release, with a new Cosmos-Reason2 backbone and deployment support.
The 1.5 report extends the Gemini Robotics line through motion transfer and reasoning/action interleaving.
Robotics 2 extends the earlier upper-body focus into whole-body control.
ER 1.6 follows ER 1.5 within the reasoning branch; it does not replace the VLA action decoder.
edges.endpoint_note: The combined source card covers ER1.5 and VLA1.5; this particular successor edge is explicitly the ER branch.

edges.explanation: ER 2 is the later embodied reasoning model in the same family, now based on Gemini 3.5 Flash.
ER 2 supplies planning and coordination while Robotics 2 produces executable robot behavior.
The On-Device 2 model card explicitly names Robotics 1.5 technology and on-device Gemma as its basis.
RDT scales continuous generative action modeling and adds unified physical action semantics; comparison is methodological, not weight inheritance.
OpenDriveLab UniVLA explicitly acknowledges OpenVLA code; its defining change is learning task-centric latent actions from video.
Two independently authored UniVLA papers have different arXiv IDs, repositories, architectures and objectives.
Both need canonical physical action mappings across embodiments; no direct RDT checkpoint inheritance is claimed.
Soft prompts and embodiment adapters are alternative ways to separate shared representations from hardware-specific interfaces.
RTC is introduced for action-chunking flow policies and addresses latency without replacing semantic pretraining.
N1.6 reports using real-time chunking during asynchronous robot rollouts.
Observation-conditioned planning extends grounding beyond language relevance and affordance scoring; no weight inheritance asserted.
Fixed skill selection versus geometry-grounded waypoint synthesis.
Both connect multimodal reasoning to low-level execution through explicit intermediate interfaces.
Multimodal motor policy versus multimodal textual planner.
Contrastive temporal alignment versus MAE-based broad sensorimotor evaluation; no direct weight reuse claimed.
RVT directly addresses explicit 3D compute cost and compares against PerAct.
Discrete voxel/keypose classification versus continuous geometric action diffusion.
Both exploit 3D scene structure; action parameterization and attention differ.
GR-2 scales generative video pretraining and joint video-action modeling in the GR family.
Action-conditioned predictor is post-trained using robot trajectories on V-JEPA 2 features.
2.1 adds dense/deep supervision and joint image/video scaling.

V-JEPA 2.1 robot experiments reuse 2-AC predictor architecture, public code and planning protocol, but retrain the action-conditioned predictor on DROID with the new encoder; no inherited predictor weights are claimed.
Official Genie series progression; exact weight inheritance not stated.
Official next-generation interactive environment model; architecture reuse not asserted.
Both support policy learning from imagined experience; video simulation and compact reward-driven latent RL have different interfaces.
Both couple future observations and actions; Cosmos Policy additionally models values for optional search.
Both unify prediction and action; Cosmos 3 is a different reasoner/generator architecture, not established as a Policy checkpoint successor.
Cosmos 3 officially unifies formerly separated model lines; not a claim of direct parameter inheritance.
Wayve release describes GAIA lineage and evaluation focus.
GAIA-4 extends driver-in-the-loop simulation and coherent radar/camera generation.
Open-ended generated interactive worlds versus logged-scene-grounded driving counterfactual validation.
Cosmos Policy directly initializes from Cosmos-Predict2-2B-Video2World and post-trains action/state/value latent frames.
Tracking a chosen clip becomes matching a movement distribution; conceptual comparison, not weight inheritance.
ASE uses adversarial motion priors with a learnable latent skill interface for reuse.
Both track motion; PHC makes capacity allocation and recovery central. No inherited checkpoint claimed.
OmniH2O names H2O as prior work and extends the universal interface and learned autonomy.
Both use motion-following controllers to collect demonstrations for autonomous upper layers; neither is asserted to derive from the other.
Both frame broad motor competence as motion tracking, but architecture and real-robot scope differ.
Missing-motion completion and universal motion-token tracking solve adjacent interface problems; no direct lineage asserted.
Paper fine-tunes a VLA that emits teleoperation-format commands executed by SONIC; only a one-task compatibility PoC.
Current WBC repository documents collection, N1.7 fine-tuning and SONIC-backed VLA execution.
NoMaD explicitly uses ViNT to encode observations/goals before diffusion decoding.
Local learned navigation and persistent semantic object memory could be composed; the survey does not claim an implemented coupling.
GOAT-Bench formalizes multi-modal lifelong navigation evaluation; benchmark is not a successor policy.
Figure extends S2/S1 with S0 and full-body sensing/actuation.
Both place learned motor competence below goal-level reasoning, but their clock rates, interfaces and disclosure differ; no code/weight lineage claimed.
Skild presents S1 as its latest flagship foundation model, emphasizing in-context task adaptation.
Sensor/action history supports dynamics adaptation in one; demonstration context specifies tasks in the other. These are not equivalent evaluations.
Generalist describes improved context-based and few-step adaptation after the GEN-1 stage.
S1 describes episodic demonstration-conditioned pretraining; GEN-1.5 says ICL emerged from continuous physical-data pretraining without a dedicated ICL objective.
Human demonstrations, reward learning and interventions extend sample-efficient real-world RL into a practical correction loop.
GO-1 inserts a latent planner before diffusion action generation; GO-1 Air removes the planner.
The official repository identifies Molmo2-ER as the embodied reasoning backbone for a continuous action expert.
A shared action-generator family is augmented with explicit asynchronous training and runtime consistency; no weight inheritance from PI is implied.
